conservative_interpretation: In this frozen 20-circuit four-qubit validation workload on ibm_pittsburgh, the ideal simulator and physical QPU produced similar output distributions relative to the much larger discrepancy between the current CC-NQE/QuTE model and the ideal simulator. The dominant observed error source is therefore the learned model approximation, not hardware noise, within this limited experiment.

composition_ood_diagnostic.interpretation: The severe Composition-OOD failure observed in the current model cannot be primarily attributed to the hardware discrepancy measured in this experiment.

hypotheses.H_HW1: More two-qubit gates may increase physical hardware discrepancy.
hypotheses.H_HW2: Greater transpiled depth may increase physical hardware discrepancy.

allowed_claims: Current model error is much larger than measured QPU-vs-simulator discrepancy in this experiment.
The simulator remains a reasonable large-scale teacher for the current restricted workload.
Composition-OOD remains primarily a model/generalization problem in this experiment.
The observed two-qubit-gate and depth correlations are hypotheses for later hardware studies.
prohibited_claims: IBM hardware noise is negligible in general.
An ideal simulator always predicts physical QPUs accurately.
QPU validation is no longer necessary.
Twenty circuits establish universal hardware behavior.
QuTE currently approximates the QPU well.
QuTE can replace physical QPUs in its current form.
